calibration_source: PWT 10.0, Destatis VGR 2024, AMECO NAWRU, Eurostat

x_comments.alpha_K: Capital share from PWT (labor share ~0.67). Standard for Germany.
x_comments.delta_annual: 5% annual depreciation for total-economy capital (structures + equipment). PWT 10.0 composite rate for Germany ~4.5-5.5%. NOTE: This differs from the DSGE .mod file delta_k=0.025 quarterly (~9.6% annual), which represents fast-depreciating equipment for cyclical dynamics. The growth model matches total GFCF (Eurostat P51G) including slow-depreciating structures, so it needs the lower rate.
x_comments.beta_annual: Discount factor: 0.96 annual. With positive trend growth, the modified-golden-rule BGP real rate exceeds 4%; under the current Germany calibration it is about 5.3% annual.
x_comments.sigma: Inverse IES (CRRA coefficient). sigma=1.5 is mid-range consensus (1=log, 2=high risk aversion).
x_comments.tfp_growth_annual: 0.5% annual TFP growth. Conservative for Germany post-2000 (Fernald puts US at ~0.5%).
x_comments.phi: Inverse Frisch elasticity on extensive margin. Controls slope of participation response to wages. Higher phi = less elastic. phi=1.3 calibrated from SimPaths response surface (4 permanent wage-shift experiments: 0/5/10/15%, grand mean eps_L=0.773, phi=1/eps_L=1.29, rounded to 1.3). See analyze_phi.py and scoping doc Section 3.2.
x_comments.labor_supply: Default Ramsey labor-supply mode. calibrate_growth_model.m copies this template into the bundle folder input/DE/MacroModel/ and writes the calibrated runtime fields there.

base_year_values.WAP_comment: Working-age population (15-64), thousands. Source: Eurostat demo_pjan, Germany 2000. Must match build_population_projection.m age range.
base_year_values.x_comment: calibrate_growth_model.m writes calibrated base-year levels and derived fields into input/DE/MacroModel/growth_params_Germany.json.

inflation_target.x_comment: ECB 2% target. rho=0.95 for pre-EMU convergence (irrelevant for DE post-2000). pi_star entered as annual percent.

labor_trends.nawru_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample ILO unemployment rate, written by calibrate_growth_model.m. Intended source: AMECO.
labor_trends.demographic_L_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample labour force, written by calibrate_growth_model.m; no projection tail. Intended source: Eurostat population projections + Destatis labor force participation.
labor_trends.x_comment: nawru_file is read for diagnostics only. demographic_L_file has no post-sample tail, so ramsey_trend.m extends N at its trailing 20-quarter trend growth rate, untapered, until build_population_projection.m supplies a projection. Hours: log-linear trend fitted to observed.

solver.x_comment: Stacked-time Newton (LBJ) perfect-foresight solver with terminal K/Y closure. The solve runs over the observed sample plus a terminal tail of 400 quarters (~100 years); Newton convergence requires ||F||_inf <= 1.0e-10 within 200 iterations.
